claims.text: DFT-based simulations can effectively achieve phase stability, microstructure refinement, and property optimization in materials with variable composition and microstructure.
The proposed intervention consists of DFT-based simulations using ab initio calculations or molecular dynamics simulations.
Electronic structure and atomic arrangement mediate the effects of the simulations.
Simulation-driven prediction enables optimization of material properties.
The intervention will improve phase stability by 20% relative to trial-and-error approaches.
The intervention will refine the microstructure by 15% relative to trial-and-error approaches.
The intervention will improve desired properties by 10% relative to trial-and-error approaches.
The stated applicability boundary is materials with fixed composition and microstructure.
The accuracy of DFT-based simulations may be limited by the selected exchange-correlation functional.
The accuracy of DFT-based simulations may be limited by material-system complexity.
Limitations in simulation accuracy could affect the predicted improvements.
An improvement of less than 5% relative to trial-and-error approaches is defined as falsifying the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis and initial state concern materials with variable composition and microstructure, whereas the stated boundary identifies materials with fixed composition and microstructure, leaving the intended domain internally inconsistent.
